anomalies.observed: ESP32-C3 EN/CHIP_PU pin (U1 pin 8) is on the GND net. R5 (10k) sits directly between GND (pin 1) and +3V3 (pin 2), so it is not connected to the EN pin at all. EN is held permanently low, which keeps the chip in reset.
anomalies.expected: EN should be pulled high to +3V3 through a 10k pull-up (the usual ESP32 reset/enable arrangement), with the pull-up's free end on the EN net. R5 is the obvious candidate for that pull-up, but its pin 1 is on GND rather than on the EN net.
anomalies.impact: With EN tied to ground the MCU never leaves reset, so the firmware never runs: no thermocouple reads, no heater control, and no Wi-Fi. The 10k resistor also just bleeds 3.3 V to ground continuously.

anomalies.observed: C7 (10uF, 0805) has both pins on the GND net, so it is shorted across itself and does nothing. Its LCSC field is also malformed ("LCSC`").
anomalies.expected: A bulk decoupling capacitor on the MCU supply would have one terminal on +3V3 and one on GND. The spec lists the 3.3 V decoupling caps (C3/C4/C6/C8/C9/C10/C12) and does not mention C7.
anomalies.impact: The intended 10uF decoupling on the MCU rail is missing, which could mean less supply stability for the ESP32 during Wi-Fi transmit bursts. The shorted part is a harmless dead component but indicates a wiring error.
